entries.text: Missing Ownership Check in Kibana Security AI Assistant Shared-conversation Deletion Missing authorization in the Elastic AI Assistant for Security in Kibana can allow an authenticated assistant user to permanently delete a shared or global Security AI Assistant conversation owned by another user in the same space. The individual-delete path can treat read access to a shared conversation as permission to delete it without checking ownership. The deleted conversation history is lost to its legitimate owner. Affected Versions: 9.x: All versions from 9.2.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Affected Configurations: Exploitation requires an authenticated user with the Elastic AI Assistant: All feature privilege for the Security AI Assistant in the affected Kibana space, and a shared or global Security AI Assistant conversation owned by another user. Deployments where no account has this effective privilege do not meet the exploitation requirements, even though the affected component is included with Kibana. When assessing access, include privileges granted through built-in roles or broader Kibana privileges. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 9.5.7. entries.summary: Elasticsearch Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') Vulnerability An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop.
entries.text: Elasticsearch Unreachable Exit Condition ('Infinite Loop') Vulnerability An issue was discovered in Elasticsearch where specially crafted compressed payloads can cause an infinite loop. A low-privileged authenticated user can submit a malformed payload to a product API endpoint that causes the node to enter a permanent CPU loop, occupying a request-processing thread indefinitely. This can progressively exhaust the node's processing capacity, degrading or denying access to product features, and requiring a restart of the affected node to recover. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.25 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.9 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.26, 9.4.10, and 9.5.7. entries.text: Elasticsearch Uncontrolled Resource Consumption Uncontrolled resource consumption in Elasticsearch query parsing can lead to denial of service. An authenticated user with search permissions can submit a specially crafted query containing an excessive number of clauses. Expanding those clauses in memory before enforcing query complexity limits can exhaust heap memory and crash an Elasticsearch node. entries.text: Privilege Escalation via Directly Uploaded Integration Packages in Kibana An issue in Kibana allows Elasticsearch transforms in directly uploaded integration packages to run with Kibana's internal system identity instead of the installing user's privileges. A user with Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges in a single Kibana space could access or modify data they are not authorized to access, including agent policies from other spaces. This could disclose sensitive information or lead to command execution on managed Elastic Agent hosts. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.14.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.9 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: The attacker has both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges in at least one Kibana space. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.10, and 9.5.6. Uninstall affected packages whose transforms retain Kibana's internal system authorization, then reinstall any packages still needed after upgrading so their transforms use the installing user's privileges. entries.text: Missing Ownership Check in Kibana AI Assistant Conversation Deletion Missing authorization in Kibana Security AI Assistant conversation deletion can allow an authenticated user with access to the assistant to delete other users' conversations in the same space. The delete-all operation can issue a query without an ownership filter using the assistant's internal Elasticsearch client. A user can consequently delete conversation history that they do not own or have permission to modify. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.19.0 up to and including 8.19.25 9.x: All versions from 9.1.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Affected Configurations: Exploitation requires the Elastic AI Assistant feature privilege (`elasticAssistant`) in the affected Kibana space. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.26 and 9.5.7. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Remove the Elastic AI Assistant feature privilege from untrusted roles until upgrading to a fixed version. entries.text: Kibana Exposure of Sensitive Information Certain Fleet APIs in Kibana expose stored credentials to authenticated users who do not have the Fleet Settings: Read privilege. For example, a user with the Fleet Agent policies: Read privilege can retrieve credentials through Fleet output and agent binary download source APIs. The disclosed credentials could allow the attacker to authenticate to connected backend systems. entries.text: Missing Authorization in Kibana Cases Alert Attachments Missing authorization in Kibana Cases alert attachments can allow an authenticated user with permission to add case comments or attachments to modify case-link metadata in documents they are not authorized to access. An attacker can add false case links and prevent legitimate case linkage by exhausting the alert's case-link limit. Writes are limited to the kibana.alert.case_ids field in indices that Kibana's internal account can read and update and whose mappings accept that field. One of the two authorization defects was fixed earlier in 8.19.22, 9.4.8 and 9.5.5; the fixed versions listed in this advisory address both defects. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: The attacker must have Cases read and create_comment (Create comments & attachments) privileges, or Cases all, for the Cases feature matching the case owner in the affected space: generalCasesV3, securitySolutionCasesV3 or observabilityCasesV3. The attacker must have access to an existing case where they can add an attachment, or permission to create such a case. entries.summary: Buffer Over-read in Elasticsearch LZ4 Transport Decompression A buffer over-read vulnerability in Elasticsearch transport decompression can expose data from other requests.
entries.text: Buffer Over-read in Elasticsearch LZ4 Transport Decompression A buffer over-read vulnerability in Elasticsearch transport decompression can expose data from other requests. The LZ4 decoder can read beyond the declared compressed block into a shared network buffer. A remote attacker who can reach an affected transport interface can send a specially crafted compressed request and obtain data from outside their own request. Exploitation of the exposed remote-cluster transport interface does not require authentication. Affected Versions: 7.x: All versions from 7.14.0 up to and including 7.17.29 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: There is no complete workaround. To reduce exposure until upgrading, keep the node-to-node transport and remote-cluster transport ports private, enforce mutual TLS on those ports, and restrict access to trusted source addresses using xpack.security.transport.filter.* and xpack.security.remote_cluster.filter.*. These controls limit access by untrusted callers and do not replace upgrading to a fixed version. Elastic Cloud Hosted Elastic deployed a proxy-side mitigation to all Elastic Cloud Hosted environments before disclosure. Customers running affected Elasticsearch versions should still upgrade to a fixed version

entries.summary: Relative Path Traversal in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent A relative path traversal vulnerability in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent allows an authenticated user with both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All…
entries.text: Relative Path Traversal in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent A relative path traversal vulnerability in Kibana Fleet and Elastic Agent allows an authenticated user with both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges to distribute a malicious integration policy to managed Elastic Agents. A vulnerable Elastic Agent processing that policy for a component that runs in an isolated unit can modify or delete files outside the component's intended runtime directory with the privileges of the Elastic Agent process. This can cause loss of files or persistent denial of service on affected hosts. Affected Versions: Kibana 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.24 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.9 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Elastic Agent / Fleet-managed isolated-unit components 8.x: All versions from 8.15.0 up to and including 8.19.21 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.6 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.3 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: The Kibana Fleet feature is enabled. The attacker is authenticated and has both Fleet Integrations: All and Agent policies: All privileges. A vulnerable Fleet-managed Elastic Agent processes the policy for a component whose units are isolated, such as Cloud Security Posture (Cloudbeat). Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in Kibana versions 8.19.25, 9.4.10, and 9.5.7

entries.summary: Cross-user Data Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow Responses A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests.
entries.text: Cross-user Data Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow Responses A pooled-buffer lifetime error in Elasticsearch ES|QL Arrow response formatting can disclose data from other users' concurrent requests. An authenticated user with read access to an index who requests Arrow output containing an affected column type can receive data from indices they are not authorized to access. A temporary block can be released to a shared memory pool before deferred response writers finish using it, allowing concurrent requests to reuse the same memory. The attacker cannot select which concurrent data is disclosed. Affected Versions: Elasticsearch / ES|QL 8.x: All versions from 8.15.0 up to and including 8.19.24 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: ES|QL responses are requested with format=arrow and contain an affected column type: ip, version, _source, or flattened (flattened from 9.5). Other users' requests execute concurrently. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.25, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. Severity: CVSSv3.1: Medium ( 5.3 ) - CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:H/PR:L/UI:N/S:U/C:H/I:N/A:N CVE ID: CVE-2026-133930 Problem Type: CWE-416 - Use After Free 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic

entries.text: Unconstrained S3 Endpoints in Elasticsearch ES|QL Data Sources Unconstrained S3 endpoint settings in Elasticsearch ES|QL data sources can cause requests containing storage credentials to be sent to an attacker-controlled host. A user with data-source management privileges can configure a custom endpoint without the intended host restriction. On opted-in commercial Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments, the issue can also disclose workload-identity tokens and expose customer cloud resources outside Elasticsearch. Self-managed deployments are affected by the storage-endpoint path only. Affected Versions: Elasticsearch / ES|QL 9.x: All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: ES|QL federation is enabled. The attacker has data-source management privileges. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 9.5.6. After upgrading, data sources using non-AWS endpoints require an operator to add the trusted host to esql.external.allowed_endpoint_hosts. This is a node setting and requires a restart; until configured, affected custom-endpoint data sources stop serving reads. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Leave esql.federation.enabled disabled. Where federation is enabled, review the endpoint and sts_endpoint settings of existing S3 data sources and restrict data-source management privileges to trusted administrators. entries.summary: Credential Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Data-source Audit Logging Elasticsearch ES|QL data-source and dataset registration can write storage credentials or pre-signed URL signatures to the audit log in plaintext.
entries.text: Credential Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Data-source Audit Logging Elasticsearch ES|QL data-source and dataset registration can write storage credentials or pre-signed URL signatures to the audit log in plaintext. In affected versions, request definitions are not appropriately filtered before request-body or URL-query auditing. An attacker with access to these logs can obtain credentials for the customer's external storage. The issue affects deployments with ES|QL federation enabled and audit logging configured to record the affected request information. Affected Versions: Elasticsearch / ES|QL 9.x: All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: ES|QL federation is enabled. Audit logging is enabled; request-body disclosure additionally requires request-body audit logging. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 9.5.7. Rotate data-source credentials that may have been written to audit logs and review access to retained copies. Do not submit credentials in URL query parameters. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Disable ES|QL federation and keep esql.federation.enabled disabled until the fixed version is installed. If federation was enabled together with affected audit logging, rotate the data-source credentials and review access to retained audit logs. entries.text: Storage-location Disclosure in Elasticsearch ES|QL Query Responses Elasticsearch ES|QL query responses can disclose dataset storage locations and provider identity details to users who are allowed to query a dataset but cannot read its definition. Storage paths and storage-client error text can appear in read-failure messages or query-profile plan strings. An authenticated dataset reader can obtain this information without permission to view the dataset configuration. This issue does not disclose stored credentials or the dataset contents beyond the caller's query access. Affected Versions: Elasticsearch / ES|QL 9.x: All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.6 Affected Configurations: The vulnerability affects deployments that meet all of the following conditions: ES|QL federation is enabled. The caller can read a dataset but is not authorized to read its definition. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 9.5.7. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Leave esql.federation.enabled disabled. Where federation is enabled, grant dataset read access only to users who may know the underlying storage location. entries.text: Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value in Packetbeat Leading to Denial of Service Memory Allocation with Excessive Size Value (CWE-789) in Packetbeat can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted, malformed Cassandra protocol message. An unauthenticated attacker who can send traffic on a network segment that Packetbeat monitors can cause Packetbeat to allocate excessive memory and terminate. Elastic Agent is also affected when the Network Packet Capture integration monitors Cassandra traffic, because it uses the same protocol decoder. Elastic Agent with the Network Packet Capture integration and its Cassandra data stream enabled. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in Packetbeat versions 8.19.25, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. entries.summary: We’re changing the identifier format for new Elastic Security Advisories published in Security Announcements. Going forward, ESA IDs will use the format ESA-YYYY-xxxx-xxxx, for example ESA-2026-7gxm-4cqw.
entries.text: We’re changing the identifier format for new Elastic Security Advisories published in Security Announcements. Going forward, ESA IDs will use the format ESA-YYYY-xxxx-xxxx, for example ESA-2026-7gxm-4cqw. The suffix contains eight randomly generated characters in two groups of four, replacing the sequential number. Previously published ESA IDs will remain valid and unchanged. You can continue to use them when referencing historical advisories. If you have automation that parses ESA IDs, please update it to support the new format alongside historical IDs. The following regular expression is the exact pattern used by our schema for new IDs: ^ESA-\d{4}-[23456789cfghjmpqrvwx]{4}-[23456789cfghjmpqrvwx]{4}$ The suffix is lowercase and uses only the characters shown in the pattern. New IDs do not indicate publication order. 1 post - 1 participant Read full topic

entries.summary: Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Elastic Cloud Enterprise Java4Shell Remote Code Execution and Denial of Service CVE-2026-114938, also known as Java4Shell, is a vulnerability in OpenJDK and Oracle Java SE disclosed on…
entries.text: Elasticsearch, Logstash, and Elastic Cloud Enterprise Java4Shell Remote Code Execution and Denial of Service CVE-2026-114938, also known as Java4Shell, is a vulnerability in OpenJDK and Oracle Java SE disclosed on November 17, 2026. For Elasticsearch and Logstash, only nodes on x86-64 CPUs that support the AVX512_VBMI instruction set are affected. Nodes on ARM CPUs and on older x86 CPUs are not affected at this time. In Elasticsearch, an authenticated user with at least read access can exploit the vulnerability to achieve remote code execution. Unauthenticated attackers can exploit it to cause denial of service against Elasticsearch nodes. In Logstash, an unauthenticated attacker who can submit events from an untrusted source can cause denial of service when the Elastic Integration filter (logstash-filter-elastic_integration) runs an Elasticsearch ingest pipeline that decodes attacker-controlled Base64 fields. The impact in Logstash is a process crash, not code execution. The Logstash API, Ruby plugins, and common inputs such as Beats, HTTP, and TCP do not use the affected Java function. Logstash 7.17.x and versions before 8.6.2 are not affected at this time. entries.text: Out-of-bounds Write in Elastic Maps Server Leading to Remote Code Execution Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) in the Brotli decoder used by the Node.js runtime, a dependency of Elastic Maps Server (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to corrupt memory and potentially execute code in the Elastic Maps Server process via a specially crafted, malformed compressed response from Elasticsearch. Exploitation requires an attacker who controls the response from the Elasticsearch cluster that Elastic Maps Server connects to. The issue is tracked as CVE-2026-111497. The Elastic Maps Server Docker images include an affected version of the Brotli library. Elastic confirmed that the vulnerable decoder is reachable in Elastic Maps Server but did not reproduce memory corruption or code execution in Elastic Maps Server. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: All Elastic Maps Server Docker images of the affected versions include an affected version of the Brotli library. Elastic Maps Server decodes Brotli-compressed responses only from the configured Elasticsearch host, for example during the license check. entries.text: Improper Certificate Validation in Elastic Docker Images Leading to Interception of TLS Connections Improper Certificate Validation (CWE-295) in the operating system certificate bundle shipped in the Docker images of APM Server Auditbeat, Filebeat, Heartbeat, Metricbeat and Packetbeat Elastic Agent, including Fleet Server and Cloudbeat Logstash, for TLS connections that use the operating system certificate bundle Elastic connectors Universal Profiling (host agent, collector and symbolizer) Elastic Maps Server A dependency of these products (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to intercept or modify TLS-protected traffic via Signature Spoofing by Key Theft (CAPEC-474). The certificate bundle includes root certificate authorities that signed eight eMudhra intermediate certificate authorities whose private keys are compromised. Anyone with these keys can issue a certificate for any host name that these products accept as trusted. Exploitation requires an attacker in a network position between the product and the remote party, who presents a certificate issued with one of the compromised keys. entries.summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in APM Server Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized…
entries.text: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in APM Server Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in APM Server can lead to denial of service via Oversized Serialized Data Payloads (CAPEC-231). An attacker who can send OpenTelemetry (OTLP) data to APM Server over HTTP can cause APM Server to exhaust its memory and terminate. This stops the intake of APM and OpenTelemetry data until APM Server restarts. The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. The fixed versions reject OTLP/HTTP requests with a body larger than 64 MiB after decompression, as recommended by the OTLP specification. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.3.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: All APM Server deployments, standalone and Fleet-managed, are affected. OTLP/HTTP intake is enabled by default. OTLP/gRPC intake is not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in versions 8.19.24, 9.4.9, and 9.5.6. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: There are no workarounds for this vulnerability. Indicators of Compromise (IOC) No specific indicators of compromise have been identified for this vulnerability. entries.summary: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in Elasticsearch Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via a…
entries.text: Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling in Elasticsearch Leading to Denial of Service Allocation of Resources Without Limits or Throttling (CWE-770) in Elasticsearch can lead to denial of service via a specially crafted input value that is processed by an affected phonetic encoder of the analysis-phonetic plugin. An authenticated user with permission to write documents to or run searches against an index that uses an affected encoder can cause an Elasticsearch node to exhaust its heap memory. The node can become unresponsive or terminate. Affected Versions: 8.x: All versions from 8.0.0 up to and including 8.19.23 9.x: All versions from 9.0.0 up to and including 9.4.8 All versions from 9.5.0 up to and including 9.5.5 Affected Configurations: Clusters that have the analysis-phonetic plugin installed and at least one index with an analyzer that uses the koelnerphonetik or haasephonetik encoder. Other phonetic encoders are not affected. Clusters without the analysis-phonetic plugin are not affected. Solutions and Mitigations: The issue is resolved in version 8.19.24, 9.4.9 and 9.5.6. For Users that Cannot Upgrade: Stop using the koelnerphonetik and haasephonetik encoders in index analyzers. To change the analyzer of an existing field, create a new index with an updated mapping and reindex the data into it. This workaround applies to self-managed and Elastic Cloud Hosted deployments. entries.text: Out-of-bounds Write in Elastic Agent Leading to Remote Code Execution Out-of-bounds Write (CWE-787) in the Brotli decoder of Node.js, a dependency of Elastic Agent (Dependency on Vulnerable Third-Party Component, CWE-1395), could allow an attacker to cause a crash, disclose process memory, or potentially execute code within the Node.js process that runs Synthetics browser monitors via a specially crafted, malformed compressed response. Exploitation requires an attacker who controls an endpoint that a journey requests, or who has compromised an upstream service, to return a response that triggers the known vulnerability CVE-2026-111497. If code execution succeeds, the attacker gains the same access to files, credentials, and network resources as the affected Synthetics process. The Elastic Agent Docker images that support Synthetics browser monitors bundle Node.js as the Synthetics monitoring runtime.
